title: Oxidation, Reduction and Half-equations
seo_title: Year 12 Chemistry: Oxidation and Reduction Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Oxidation and reduction as electron transfer; oxidation numbers; oxidising and reducing agents; half-equations in acid; the reactivity series and displacement reactions; corrosion and its prevention; redox titrations. (Senior Secondary Chemistry, Unit 3: Equilibrium, acids and redox reactions)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Chemistry worksheets on redox: oxidation numbers, oxidising and reducing agents, half-equations, the reactivity series, displacement, corrosion and redox titrations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).
key_sub: Balance half-equations: atoms, then O with H₂O, H with H⁺, charge with e⁻.
body_html:
How to think about it

Oxidation is the loss of electrons (oxidation number goes up); reduction is the gain of electrons (oxidation number goes down). The oxidising agent is reduced; the reducing agent is oxidised.

A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from solution. To balance a half-equation in acid: balance the element, add H₂O for oxygen, H⁺ for hydrogen and electrons for charge. Corrosion is oxidation of metals; sacrificial anodes and galvanising protect steel.

Example

Oxidation number of Mn in MnO₄⁻?

x + 4 × (−2) = −1

Answer: +7

Example

Balance MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ in acid

add 4H₂O on the right

add 8H⁺ on the left

add 5e⁻ on the left

Answer: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O

Common mistakes

  • Saying the oxidising agent is oxidised.
  • Forgetting to balance charge with electrons.
  • Thinking a less reactive metal can displace a more reactive one.

faq.q: How do you identify oxidation and reduction?
faq.a: Work out oxidation numbers: the element whose number rises is oxidised; the one whose number falls is reduced.

faq.q: Why does galvanised iron not rust even when scratched?
faq.a: Zinc is more reactive, so it is oxidised instead of the iron (sacrificial protection).

items.q: A piece of lead is placed in aluminium nitrate solution. Will a displacement reaction occur? (Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au)
c: No. Metals never react with solutions.
Yes. Any metal replaces any other metal.
No. Lead is less active than aluminium, so no reaction occurs.
Yes. Lead is more active than aluminium, so it replaces it.
items.e: A metal replaces only metals below it in the reactivity series.

items.q: Why are blocks of magnesium or zinc attached to ship hulls?
c: they corrode instead of the steel hull (sacrificial anodes)
items.e: They are replaced as they wear away.
